title: If You Connect Your Sink Straight to the Sewer...
sources: InterNACHI 'Sewer Gases in the Home' / Wikipedia 'Sewer gas': sewer gas is a mix that includes hydrogen sulfide (rotten-egg smell) and methane; it enters homes through dry or missing traps

Wikipedia 'Trap (plumbing)' / Oatey 'What is a P-trap and how does it work' / engineerfix 'How a P-Trap Works to Prevent Sewer Gas': the U-shaped bend keeps a plug of water (the trap seal) that blocks sewer gas while letting waste water pass

2021 International Plumbing Code 1002.4 'Trap seals' (ICC) / IRC P3201.2 (jaspector) / ICC Building Safety Journal 'Overview of plumbing trap requirements': each fixture trap must have a liquid seal of not less than 2 inches and not more than 4 inches

ASHI Reporter 'Plumbing Vents - Why Basins Sometimes Talk Back' / Wikipedia 'Drain-waste-vent system' / The Physics of Siphonage (Advanced Heat & AC): water rushing down a drain pulls a vacuum that can siphon the trap empty; the vent pipe through the roof lets air in so the seal stays
Paladin Home Inspections 'What are those white pipes on the roof' / CivoPilot 'What does a roof pipe do': the small pipes on a roof are the plumbing vent stacks

RectorSeal 'How to Deal with Infrequently Used Floor Drains' / Roto-Rooter 'What happens if I have an unused bathroom drain' / Wikipedia 'Trap primer': in a rarely used drain the trap water evaporates and sewer smell comes back; pouring water in refills the seal

lines.text: If you connect your sink straight to the sewer, your house will stink like rotten eggs.
lines.caps: If you connect your sink | straight to the sewer, | your house will stink | like rotten eggs.

lines.text: Because sewer pipes are full of gas, like hydrogen sulfide and methane.
lines.caps: Because sewer pipes | are full of gas, | like hydrogen sulfide | and methane.

lines.text: So, plumbers bend the pipe under your sink, into a U.
lines.caps: So, plumbers bend the pipe | under your sink, | into a U.

lines.text: Water stays trapped in the bend, and blocks the gas like a plug.
lines.caps: Water stays trapped | in the bend, | and blocks the gas | like a plug.

lines.text: It's called a P-trap, and the code wants two to four inches of water in it.
lines.caps: It's called a P-trap, | and the code wants | 2 to 4 inches | of water in it.

lines.text: But when a full sink drains fast, it can suck that water right out.
lines.caps: But when a full sink | drains fast, | it can suck that water | right out.

lines.text: So, a vent pipe runs up through your roof, and lets air in behind the water.
lines.caps: So, a vent pipe | runs up through your roof, | and lets air in | behind the water.

lines.text: That's the little pipe you see sticking out of your roof.
lines.caps: That's the little pipe | you see sticking out | of your roof.

lines.text: But in a drain that nobody uses, the water slowly dries up.
lines.caps: But in a drain | that nobody uses, | the water slowly dries up.

lines.text: And the sewer smell comes right back.
lines.caps: And the sewer smell | comes right back.

lines.text: So, just pour some water down it, and the seal is back.
lines.caps: So, just pour | some water down it, | and the seal is back.

lines.text: You see, the only thing between your home and the sewer is a few inches of water.
lines.caps: You see, the only thing | between your home | and the sewer | is a few inches of water.

lines.text: That's why there's a weird bend under every sink.
lines.caps: That's why there's | a weird bend | under every sink.
